title: Diagnose the mistake
summary: Work out why you got a question wrong, so that you practise the right thing next.

sections.title: Why was it wrong?
content: Think of a test question you got wrong. Writing ‘wrong’ next to it tells you nothing about what to do next.
Two students can miss the same question for different reasons, and they need different practice.

sections.title: Four reasons for a mistake
content: Knowledge: I did not know the word, rule or pattern. Reasoning: I knew the language but did not connect the clues correctly.
Attention: I knew it but misread the question or copied the wrong answer. Time: I knew how to do it but did not have enough time.
Each reason needs different practice. Knowledge needs learning. Reasoning needs slower working with evidence. Attention needs a checking routine. Time needs timed practice.

sections.title: Use the four reasons
content: Take this: ‘Sinta chose the wrong word because she thought “fragile” meant “heavy”.’ She did not know the word, so it is a knowledge error, and she should learn it with an example sentence.
Take this: ‘Eko knew all the words, but he answered from one sentence and missed the next one, which changed the meaning.’ That is a reasoning error, so he should read on before he answers.

sections.title: Name the reason
content: Read each short case and choose the reason. Look for what the student knew and what went wrong.

sections.title: Choose the next step
content: Now choose the reason or the most useful next step. Ask what would prevent this mistake next time.

sections.title: Keep a mistake log
content: For each wrong answer, write the question number, the reason and one next step. Look for the reason that appears most often.
Be honest. Calling every mistake ‘careless’ hides what you need to learn.

sections.title: Try a new case
content: Read one new case and choose the reason and next step together. If you need a hint or get it wrong, you will try a different case.
